chunks.text:
The purpose of this policy handbook is to establish clear expectations regarding employee conduct, attendance, reporting chain of command, confidentiality, ethical standards, and workplace responsibilities at BSmile The Mind Studio.
All employees are required to read, understand, and comply with the provisions outlined in this handbook. This policy is applicable to all employees working for Bsmile The Mind Studio.

Employees of BSmile The Mind Studio shall uphold:
• Integrity in Practice
• Trust & Transparency
• Respect & Compassion
• Continuous Learning & Curiosity
• Creative Problem-Solving
• Passion for Excellence
• Client-Centred Practice
• Responsible Ownership

Employees are expected to:
• Treat all clients, caregivers, visitors, and colleagues with dignity and respect.
• Maintain professional boundaries with clients at all times.
• Conduct themselves in a manner that protects the reputation of the organization.
• Refrain from any behavior that may compromise client welfare or organizational
integrity.
• Employees are expected to maintain a clean, professional, and client-appropriate
appearance while office hours and at any events representing the organization.
• Employees shall not report to work under the influence of alcohol, illegal substances,
or medications that significantly impair professional performance.
• Employees shall not bring personal visitors into therapy rooms, assessment areas, or
spaces containing confidential client information.

Moonlighting, secondary employment (Exception for Online psychologists), freelance work, consulting assignments, or any paid professional engagement outside BSmile The Mind Studio is strictly prohibited.
This includes:
• Providing therapy services independently.
• Working for competing organizations.
• Conducting private consultations for remuneration.
• Online counselling or coaching services outside organizational authorization.
Violation of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.
Any exceptional circumstances require prior written approval from Management.

All employees must record attendance through the organization's attendance system.
• Attendance must be marked upon arrival and departure.
• Attendance should also be marked in the attendance ledger.
• Employees are responsible for ensuring successful attendance registration.
Any discrepancy, missed record, or system error must be reported immediately to the Assistant Manager via email.
Failure to report discrepancies promptly may result in the attendance being recorded as absent.

Office Working hours will be from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, including a 1-hour lunch break.
The office will be operational 6 days a week, Monday to Saturday, with Sunday as the weekly holiday. Public holidays as observed by the organization will also be considered holidays.
Employees are expected to:
• Report to work on time.
• Adhere to assigned schedules.
• Complete assigned duties during working hours.
Repeated tardiness or unauthorized absence may lead to disciplinary action.

All leave requests must be submitted through email.
Leave shall be considered approved only after Email confirmation is received from the authorized approving authority.
Employees shall not proceed on leave without approval except in genuine emergencies.
Verbal approvals are not considered official unless subsequently documented.
You will be entitled to 1 casual leave per month, subject to the organization's leave procedures and prior approval from the management.
Please note, Any Additional leaves shall be considered Leave without Pay.

chunks.sectionTitle: Extended Leave and Multiple Employee Leave
chunks.text:
Manager approval shall also be required in the following situations:
• Leave exceeding one working day.
• Multiple employees requesting leave on the same day.
Approval may be denied or modified based on service requirements and staffing needs.

In emergencies:
• The employee must inform the reporting authority immediately.
• An email notification must be sent as soon as possible.

Interns → Assistant Manager
Sales Coordinator/Sales Head → Assistant Manager/General Manager/Director (only under
management’s instruction)
Psychologist → Assistant Manager/General Manager
Online Part-Time Psychologists → Psychologist/Assistant Manager
Assistant Manager → General Manager/Director (only under management’s instruction)
General Manager → Director

Employees are expected to communicate through their immediate reporting authority.
Direct communication with higher levels of management should be avoided unless:
• Directed by management.
• Required for urgent operational reasons.
• Existing reporting channels are unavailable.

Escalation beyond the reporting hierarchy shall occur only in exceptional circumstances including:
• Client safety concerns.
• Ethical violations.
• Legal concerns.
• Serious workplace misconduct.
• Urgent operational disruptions.
Employees must attempt resolution through the normal chain of command before escalating whenever reasonably possible.

Protecting client confidentiality is a fundamental responsibility.
Employees shall:
• Maintain strict confidentiality regarding all client information.
• Access client records only when required for professional duties.
• Avoid discussing client information in public or unauthorized settings.
• Secure all documents, records, and electronic information.
Confidential information shall not be disclosed without:
• Client consent
• Legal requirement
• Clinical necessity approved by management.
Violation of confidentiality may result in immediate disciplinary action.

All clinical staff must maintain accurate and timely documentation.
Records shall include:
• Assessment notes.
• Progress notes.
• Treatment plans.
• Follow-up records.
• Referral documentation.
Documentation must be:
• Clear and objective.
• Completed promptly.
• Stored securely and maintained according to organizational requirements.
Falsification of records is grounds for disciplinary action.

All clinical professionals shall practice according to applicable professional ethical standards.
Employees shall:
• Work within their professional scope of practice.
• Maintain professional boundaries.
• Seek supervision when necessary.
• Refer clients when appropriate expertise is unavailable.
• Any employee identifying an immediate risk to a client's safety must promptly notify
their reporting authority and follow the organization's crisis management procedures.
Any unethical conduct may lead to disciplinary proceedings.

• Employees shall not engage in personal, romantic, financial, or business relationships
with clients.
• Accepting significant gifts from clients is prohibited without management approval.
• Personal contact details of employees should not be shared unless authorized by the
organization.
• Communication with clients should occur only through approved channels.

Employees shall not:
• Share confidential client information online.
• Discuss client cases on social media.
• Represent personal opinions as organizational positions.
• Post content that damages the reputation of BSmile The Mind Studio.
Any media inquiries must be directed to Management.

Each employee shall be provided with a Job Description (JD) outlining their duties, responsibilities, reporting relationships, performance expectations, and scope of work.
Employees are expected to perform their assigned responsibilities in accordance with their JD and any reasonable instructions provided by management.
The organization reserves the right to modify job responsibilities based on operational requirements, provided such changes are communicated to the employee.

BSmile The Mind Studio is committed to maintaining a respectful and inclusive workplace.
The following are strictly prohibited:
• Harassment.
• Bullying.
• Intimidation.
• Discrimination.
• Verbal abuse.
• Sexual harassment.
Complaints will be investigated confidentially and promptly.
Retaliation against employees reporting concerns is prohibited.

Employees shall:
• Use organizational systems responsibly.
• Maintain password confidentiality.
• Protect electronic records.
• Avoid unauthorized downloading or sharing of data.
Client information shall not be stored on personal devices unless specifically authorized.

In the instance of employee resignation/termination:
• All client files must be updated.
• Ongoing cases must be handed over.
• Organization property must be returned.
• Access to systems and records must be revoked.

Employees who have workplace concerns may:
1. Discuss the issue with their immediate supervisor.
2. Escalate to the Assistant Manager if unresolved.
3. Escalate to the Manager if necessary.
4. Escalate to the Director only in exceptional circumstances.
All grievances shall be reviewed fairly and confidentially.

Violations of organizational policies may result in:
• Verbal warning.
• Written warning.
• Performance improvement plan.
• Suspension.
• Termination of employment.
Serious misconduct may result in immediate termination.
Examples include:
• Breach of confidentiality.
• Falsification of records.
• Unauthorized disclosure of information.
• Workplace harassment.
• Moonlighting.
• Gross negligence affecting client welfare.

BSmile The Mind Studio reserves the right to amend, revise, or update these policies at any time to meet operational, legal, ethical, and professional requirements.
Employees will be notified of significant policy changes.

The purpose of this Hiring & Recruitment Policy is to establish a structured, transparent and consistent process for identifying, assessing and selecting individuals for employment and professional engagement at BSmile The Mind Studio.
As a mental health organisation, BSmile recognises the importance of appointing individuals who possess the required educational qualifications, professional experience, the appropriate technical competence, professional conduct, attitude, communication skills and suitability for working within a mental health care environment.
This policy aims to ensure that recruitment decisions are based on the requirements of the position and the overall suitability of the candidate for the role and the organisation.

This policy applies to the recruitment and selection of:
• Full-time employees
• Part-time employees
• Clinical and mental health professionals
• Administrative and operational employees
• Sales and business development employees
• Marketing employees
• Management positions
• Consultants and other professional engagements
• Interns and trainees, where applicable
The recruitment process may be modified according to the nature, seniority and professional requirements of a particular position.

BSmile's hiring decisions are guided by the 3A Principle - Ability, Aptitude and Attitude.
Candidates are assessed not only on their qualifications and experience, but also on their capacity to perform, learn, adapt and contribute positively to the organisation.
• Ability: The candidate's existing knowledge, qualifications, professional competence,
technical skills and capacity to perform the responsibilities of the role.
• Aptitude: The candidate's capacity to learn, adapt, solve problems, make decisions
and develop within the role.
• Attitude: The candidate's professionalism, work ethic, communication, teamwork,
openness to feedback, responsibility and approach towards clients, colleagues and the organisation.
Candidates shall be evaluated based on qualifications, relevant experience, professional competence, skills and suitability for the requirements of the position.

Candidates appointed to clinical, mental health or other regulated professional positions shall meet the educational, professional registration, licensing and other applicable requirements relevant to the role.
The recruitment process shall be conducted using role-relevant and reasonable criteria, with candidates assessed consistently throughout the selection process.
In addition to technical competence, BSmile shall consider the candidate's suitability for the organisation's professional environment, work culture, expectations and collaborative approach.

Recruitment decisions shall be made with professionalism, integrity and transparency, and candidates shall be expected to provide accurate information and documentation throughout the recruitment process.
Candidate information, documents, interview discussions and assessment outcomes shall be treated as confidential and accessed only by authorised personnel involved in the recruitment process.
Relevant educational qualifications, professional credentials, experience and other information provided by a selected candidate may be verified before appointment.

The recruitment process shall begin when a staffing requirement or vacancy is identified.
A hiring requirement may arise due to:
• Creation of a new position
• Expansion of an existing service
• Increase in workload or client requirements
• Resignation or separation of an employee
• Replacement of an existing position
• Requirement for specialised professional expertise
• Operational or organisational requirements
Before recruitment begins, the requirement for the position shall be assessed and approved by the appropriate management authority.
The requirement shall clearly identify:
• Position title
• Department/function
• Reason for hiring
• Employment type
• Required qualifications
• Required experience
• Technical competencies
• Soft skills
• Other role-specific requirements

Before a vacancy is advertised, the requirements of the position shall be clearly defined.
The hiring team shall determine the following:
The minimum and preferred educational qualifications required for the position.

Where applicable, the candidate must possess the required professional registration, license, certification or other legally/professionally recognised credential for the position.
For clinical and allied health positions, relevant professional credentials shall be verified before appointment.
The required level and nature of professional or work experience shall be determined based on the position.
The specific knowledge and technical competencies required to perform the role.
Relevant interpersonal and professional competencies, including communication, teamwork, adaptability, professionalism, problem-solving and other role-specific requirements.
Additional requirements such as location, availability, working hours, language proficiency or other role-specific criteria may be specified where relevant to the position.

Once the requirements of the position have been finalised, an appropriate Job Description (JD) and recruitment communication shall be prepared.
The recruitment content shall, as appropriate, include:
• Position title
• Location
• Employment type
• Educational qualification
• Required experience
• Professional registration/licensing requirements
• Key responsibilities
• Required technical skills
• Required soft skills
• Application procedure
• Other relevant role-specific information
The final recruitment content shall be shared with the Marketing Team for preparation and publication of the recruitment poster or other approved recruitment material.

BSmile may use one or more appropriate recruitment channels depending on the position and recruitment requirement.
These may include:
• BSmile's LinkedIn profile
• Social media platforms
• WhatsApp status/stories
• Relevant professional or graduate groups
• Professional contacts and networks
• Employee/professional referrals
• Direct contacts
• Meta advertisements
• Other suitable job portals or recruitment platforms
The recruitment channels selected may vary according to the nature of the vacancy and the type of candidate being sought.

Applications and candidate leads received through the recruitment channels shall be reviewed against the requirements of the position.
An initial screening may be conducted through telephone or other appropriate communication with the candidate.
Candidates may be shortlisted based on:
• Educational qualifications
• Professional credentials
• Relevant work experience
• Nature and quality of previous experience
• Technical suitability
• Location, where relevant to the role
• Availability
• Communication skills
• Other position-specific requirements
Only candidates who reasonably meet the requirements of the position shall ordinarily proceed to the interview stage.

BSmile shall generally follow a two-stage interview process, subject to modification based on the position.
Stage 1 – Technical/Functional Interview The first round shall primarily assess the candidate's technical and professional competence.
For clinical, psychological, allied health or other specialised professional positions, the interview panel may include:
• A relevant BSmile professional
• A qualified/experienced professional from the respective field
• Other personnel considered appropriate by management
For example, in the recruitment of an Occupational Therapist, the first-round panel may include a BSmile psychologist and an experienced Occupational Therapist.
The technical interview may assess:
• Educational foundation
• Professional knowledge
• Practical understanding
• Previous experience
• Role-specific technical skills
• Case-based or practical understanding, where appropriate
• Professional judgement
• Problem-solving ability
• Understanding of ethical and professional responsibilities
The first round shall also assess the candidate's aptitude, attitude and ability in relation to the position.
Only candidates considered suitable following the first round shall ordinarily proceed to the second round.

Candidates who successfully clear the first-round assessment shall be forwarded for the management interview.
The second round may be conducted by the Director, Manager and/or other authorised management representatives.
The management interview shall assess areas including:
• Overall suitability for the organisation
• Professional attitude
• Communication and interpersonal skills
• Organisational expectations
• Role expectations
• Availability and joining requirements
• Compensation expectations
• Alignment between candidate expectations and BSmile's requirements
• Other management-level considerations
The management team shall make the final selection decision based on the overall assessment of the candidate.

Interviewers shall assess candidates based on criteria relevant to the position.
Depending on the role, assessment may include:
• Educational qualifications
• Relevant experience
• Technical competence
• Aptitude
• Professional attitude
• Communication
• Problem-solving ability
• Role suitability
• Professionalism
• Organisational suitability
• Compensation alignment
• Other role-specific requirements
The assessment should consider the candidate's overall suitability rather than relying solely on one factor or one stage of the interview.

Following completion of the interview process, the selected candidate shall be approved by the authorised management personnel.
The final selection shall be based on:
1. Meeting the minimum requirements of the position 2. Performance during the interview/assessment process 3. Professional and technical suitability 4. Organisational suitability 5. Verification of relevant credentials and information 6. Management approval.
No candidate shall be considered formally appointed until the required approval and appointment process has been completed.

Following selection and prior to or as part of appointment formalities, BSmile may conduct appropriate verification of the selected candidate's information.
Depending on the position, this may include verification of:
• Identity documents
• Educational qualifications
• Professional qualifications
• Professional registration/license
• Relevant certifications
• Previous employment/experience
• References, where required
• Other role-specific credentials
For clinical and professional positions, verification of applicable professional registration or licensing shall be given particular importance.
If material discrepancies, false information, forged documents or misrepresentation are identified, BSmile reserves the right to withdraw the selection or offer, subject to applicable requirements and organisational procedures.

The selected candidate shall be required to submit the documents specified by BSmile for appointment.
The required documentation may include:
• Identity proof
• Educational certificates
• Professional registration/licence
• Relevant experience certificates
• Photograph
• Bank/payment details
• Emergency contact details
The specific documentation required may vary depending on the position and employment type.

Following completion of the selection process and required approvals, BSmile shall issue an Offer Letter to the selected candidate.
The Offer Letter shall contain applicable employment or engagement terms, including:
• Designation
• Employment/engagement type
• Compensation/Salary/Stipend
• Joining date, Probation Period terms
• Working hours or applicable schedule
• Reporting structure
• Applicable terms and conditions
• Any Other relevant appointment terms
The candidate shall be required to review and accept the Offer Letter in the manner specified by BSmile.

The selected candidate shall be provided with the applicable Employee Handbook along with or during the offer and appointment process.
The candidate shall be expected to read, understand and comply with the policies, procedures, professional standards and workplace expectations contained therein.
The Employee Handbook shall operate alongside the Offer Letter and other applicable organisational policies.

Following acceptance of the Offer Letter, the candidate shall be provided with a confirmed joining date.
On or around the date of joining, BSmile shall conduct an appropriate onboarding/orientation process.
The onboarding process may include:
• Welcome and introduction to the organisation
• Introduction to the team
• Explanation of organisational structure
• Explanation of reporting hierarchy
• Introduction to relevant departments/personnel
• Explanation of organisational workflow
• Explanation of role and responsibilities
• Introduction to applicable policies,procedures and documentation.
• Other role-specific orientation or training
The extent of onboarding may vary according to the position and level of responsibility.

All candidate information obtained during recruitment shall be treated as confidential.
Recruitment information shall be shared only with personnel who are authorised or reasonably required to participate in the recruitment and selection process.
Interview discussions, candidate evaluations, personal documents and other recruitment- related information shall not be disclosed unnecessarily to unauthorised individuals.

Any person participating in the recruitment or selection process shall disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest involving a candidate.
Where a conflict may affect the fairness or objectivity of the selection process, management may reassign the relevant interviewer or decision-maker.
Personal relationships or external interests shall not improperly influence recruitment decisions.

BSmile shall seek to maintain a fair and professional recruitment process.
Employment decisions shall be based on legitimate requirements of the position, qualifications, competence, experience, professional suitability and organisational requirements.
BSmile does not discriminate on the basis of race, caste, colour, religion, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, marital status, nationality, social or economic background, or any other status protected under applicable law, except where a specific requirement is a legitimate and lawful occupational requirement.
Selection criteria shall be relevant to the position and applied consistently.

chunks.sectionTitle: RECRUITMENT OF INTERNS, CONSULTANTS AND PART-TIME
chunks.text:
PROFESSIONALS Interns, consultants and part-time professionals may be recruited through a process appropriate to the nature of their engagement.
The organisation may modify the standard recruitment process based on:
• Duration of engagement
• Nature of responsibilities
• Professional requirements
• Level of supervision
• Qualification requirements
• Scope of work
All such engagements shall be subject to applicable documentation, confidentiality requirements and organisational policies.

BSmile shall maintain appropriate recruitment records, which may include:
• Job description
• Recruitment advertisement/poster
• Candidate applications
• Shortlisting records
• Interview records/evaluations
• Selection decision
• Submitted documents
• Offer Letter
• Other relevant recruitment documentation
Recruitment records shall be maintained and accessed in accordance with organisational requirements and applicable data/privacy obligations.

Where exceptional circumstances require deviation from the standard recruitment process, such deviation shall require approval from the authorised management personnel.
Any exception should be based on a legitimate organisational requirement and should not compromise professional standards, credential requirements or the integrity of the recruitment process.

Management Management shall:
• Approve staffing requirements where applicable
• Participate in the final selection process
• Assess organisational and financial suitability
• Approve final appointments
• Approve exceptions to the recruitment process
Hiring Representative The relevant hiring representative shall:
• Identify and communicate the staffing requirement
• Define role requirements
• Participate in shortlisting and interviews
• Assess functional suitability
• Coordinate with relevant professionals where required
Marketing Team The Marketing Team shall:
• Prepare recruitment creatives based on approved recruitment requirements
• Publish recruitment content through approved channels
• Support recruitment campaigns and advertisements
Interview Panel The interview panel shall:
• Conduct objective and role-relevant assessments
• Assess technical and professional competence
• Provide appropriate feedback/recommendations
• Maintain confidentiality of candidate information
Candidate Candidates shall:
• Provide accurate and complete information
• Submit required documents
• Participate in the recruitment process in good faith
• Disclose relevant information required for appointment
• Comply with the terms of the Offer Letter and applicable organisational policies upon
joining

All recruitment activities at BSmile The Mind Studio shall be conducted in accordance with this policy, the applicable organisational policies and applicable laws, regulations and professional requirements in force from time to time.
Where a specific professional or statutory requirement applies to a position, the relevant requirement shall take precedence over a general recruitment practice.

This policy shall be reviewed periodically by the management of BSmile The Mind Studio to ensure that it remains appropriate to the organisation's operational requirements and applicable professional and regulatory requirements.
BSmile reserves the right to modify, amend or update this policy as required.
All amendments shall be communicated to the relevant personnel as appropriate.

The Internship Programme at BSmile The Mind Studio is designed to provide interns with structured professional exposure to the functioning of a mental health organization.
The programme provides supervised opportunities to develop professional competencies relevant to the intern's area of study or assigned role, including professional communication, documentation, client interaction, organizational processes, teamwork, and workplace conduct.
The internship is intended to provide practical exposure while maintaining appropriate professional, ethical, and confidentiality standards applicable to the organization's work.

This policy applies to all interns engaged by BSmile The Mind Studio, irrespective of their academic discipline, educational institution, internship duration, or assigned department.
Where an internship requires additional requirements based on the intern's academic programme, professional discipline, or specific assignment, such requirements may be communicated separately and shall be read together with this policy.

Internship opportunities may be offered to students or individuals who meet the educational, professional, or other requirements determined by BSmile The Mind Studio for the specific internship position.
The organization reserves the right to determine eligibility based on:
• Academic background.
• Relevant skills and competencies.
• Internship requirements.
• Availability of suitable supervisory resources.
• Organizational requirements.
• Any additional criteria established for a specific internship programme.

The duration of the internship will be determined by BSmile The Mind Studio based on the requirements of the internship programme and the applicable academic or institutional requirements.
The internship period, commencement date, and completion date will be communicated to the intern before the commencement of the internship.
Any extension or modification of the internship period will require approval from the organization.

The internship programme is intended to provide interns with structured professional exposure to:
• The functioning of a mental health organization.
• Professional workplace practices.
• Client interaction and communication, where applicable to the assigned role.
• Documentation and reporting procedures.
• Organizational coordination and teamwork.
• Multidisciplinary professional interaction, where applicable.
• Ethical and professional standards.
• Confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries.
• Responsibilities associated with the intern's assigned role.
The nature and extent of exposure provided to each intern may vary according to the intern's academic background, assigned responsibilities, demonstrated capability, performance, and organizational requirements.

Interns may be assigned responsibilities relevant to their area of study, assigned role, and the operational requirements of BSmile The Mind Studio.
Depending on the nature of the internship, responsibilities may include:
• Assisting with assigned administrative or operational activities.
• Assisting with client-related coordination where appropriate.
• Preparing and maintaining assigned documentation.
• Preparing reports and maintaining records as directed.
• Assisting relevant professional teams with assigned activities.
• Participating in meetings, discussions, presentations, or other designated activities.
• Supporting assigned projects or organizational initiatives.
• Conducting Initial Assessments and completing Assessment documentation.
• Carrying out other responsibilities reasonably assigned by the Internship Supervisor.

Responsibilities will not necessarily be identical for all interns.
The level and nature of responsibility assigned to an intern will be determined based on:
• Demonstrated capability.
• Quality and accuracy of work.
• Professional conduct.
• Reliability and punctuality.
• Ability to follow instructions.
• Ability to work independently where appropriate.
• Response to feedback.
• Overall performance.
An intern may initially be assigned limited or closely supervised responsibilities. Additional responsibilities may be assigned progressively when the intern demonstrates the required level of competence and reliability.
The organization reserves the right to modify, increase, reduce, or reassign responsibilities based on the intern's performance and operational requirements.

Each intern will be assigned an Internship Supervisor or designated reporting authority.
The intern is expected to:
• Report to the assigned supervisor as instructed.
• Complete assigned responsibilities within the specified timelines.
• Maintain regular communication regarding assigned work.
• Submit daily task reports, weekly reports, or other documentation as required.
• Seek clarification or professional guidance when required.
• Follow reasonable instructions provided by the supervisor or authorized members of
the organization.
• Report any difficulty, concern, or issue affecting assigned responsibilities in a timely
manner.
• Requests for leave should also be communicated with their supervisor and except for
emergency/sick leaves, intern should have prior approval from the supervising authority.
The Internship Supervisor will provide appropriate direction, supervision, and performance feedback based on the intern's responsibilities.

Where relevant to the internship role, interns may be provided supervised exposure to:
• Professional case discussions.
• Multidisciplinary coordination.
• Client intake and assessment procedures.
• Documentation and reporting practices.
• Treatment planning processes.
• Professional communication.
• Ethical practices within mental health services.
• Organizational procedures related to client services.
Such exposure will be provided only to the extent considered appropriate by the organization and the supervising professional.
Interns shall not independently undertake clinical, therapeutic, diagnostic, or other professional responsibilities that require a specific professional qualification, registration, or authorization.

The clinic operates Monday to Saturday, from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
Intern attendance requirements may vary depending on:
• Assigned responsibilities.
• Internship requirements.
• Scheduled activities.
• Supervisory requirements.
• Operational requirements of the organization.
Standard Timings for Interns are from 10AM-4PM.Interns may be required to attend during all or part of the clinic's operating hours, as required.
The expected schedule will be communicated by the Internship Supervisor or designated authority.
Regular attendance and punctuality are mandatory and will form part of the intern's overall performance assessment.

• Regular attendance is expected throughout the internship period.
• Leave must be communicated to and approved by the Internship Supervisor in
advance, except where circumstances make prior communication impractical.
• Medical leave may be subject to appropriate supporting documentation where
required.
• Unapproved absence may be recorded as a violation of internship requirements.
• Repeated absence or persistent punctuality issues may negatively affect the intern's
performance evaluation and eligibility for successful completion of the internship.
• The organization reserves the right to review the internship status of an intern in cases
of prolonged or repeated absence.

All interns are expected to maintain professional conduct throughout the internship.
Interns shall:
• Maintain professionalism in all interactions.
• Treat clients, supervisors, psychologists, colleagues, and other staff members with
respect.
• Maintain appropriate professional boundaries.
• Follow organizational policies, procedures, and instructions.
• Maintain punctuality and workplace discipline.
• Communicate professionally and respectfully.
• Take reasonable responsibility for assigned work.
• Respond appropriately to feedback and supervision.
• Avoid conduct that may adversely affect clients, staff members, or the reputation of
BSmile The Mind Studio.
• Uphold the ethical principles applicable to their area of study and professional
practice.

Interns are required to maintain a neat and professional appearance while attending the organization.
Appropriate professional attire may include:
• Indian formal wear.
• Western formal wear.
• Other neat and professionally appropriate attire suitable for a mental health
workplace.
The organization may provide additional dress requirements where necessary for specific activities or responsibilities.

Due to the sensitive nature of mental health services, interns may have access to confidential client, clinical, employee, operational, or organizational information.
All such information must be treated as strictly confidential.
Interns shall not:
• Disclose confidential information to unauthorized persons.
• Photograph or record client information without authorization.
• Copy, download, forward, or share confidential records without authorization.
• Discuss identifiable client information outside authorized professional settings.
• Use organizational or client information for personal, academic, social media, or other
purposes without prior authorization.
• Retain confidential information after completion of the internship unless specifically
authorized.
The obligation of confidentiality continues after the completion or termination of the internship.
Any breach of confidentiality may result in immediate discontinuation of the internship and may lead to further action as considered appropriate by the organization.

chunks.sectionTitle: USE OF ORGANIZATIONAL INFORMATION AND MATERIALS
chunks.text:
All documents, records, formats, internal processes, materials, data, and other information provided to interns for the purpose of their internship shall be used only for authorized internship-related activities.
Interns shall not reproduce, distribute, publish, or share organizational materials without prior authorization.
Any academic work, presentation, report, research, or other material prepared using organizational or client-related information must comply with confidentiality requirements and any specific instructions provided by the organization.

Intern performance will be assessed throughout the internship based on objective professional and work-related criteria.
The assessment may include:
• Attendance and punctuality.
• Professional behaviour.
• Conduct towards clients and staff.
• Communication and interpersonal skills.
• Ability to complete assigned responsibilities.
• Quality and accuracy of work.
• Structure, clarity, and accuracy of documentation.
• Timely submission of assigned reports.
• Compliance with reporting requirements.
• Ability to follow instructions.
• Ability to incorporate feedback.
• Initiative within the scope of assigned responsibilities.
• Ability to work effectively with the team.
• Overall professional development demonstrated during the internship.

Where applicable, the final assessment will include:
1. Final Report – Evaluation of the structure, clarity, content, accuracy, completeness, and submission discipline of the report.
2. Final Presentation – Presentation of a topic or topics assigned by the Internship Supervisor relating to the intern's area of study, psychology, social work, mental health, or other relevant professional subjects.
3. Overall Performance – Evaluation of attendance, punctuality, professional conduct, behaviour towards staff and clients, documentation, task completion, responsiveness to supervision, and overall performance during the internship.
The final report and presentation, together with the intern's overall performance throughout the internship, will form the basis of the final internship assessment.

Interns may receive feedback from the Internship Supervisor or other designated members of the organization during the internship.
Where performance does not meet the expected standard, the organization may:
• Provide corrective feedback.
• Clarify expected standards.
• Provide additional supervision.
• Modify assigned responsibilities.
• Reduce the level of independent responsibility.
• Review the intern's continuation in the programme.
